invariants.invariant: A rejection records one exact earliest-stage finding and every later-stage callback count is zero.
Only declared states and operations are eligible; stale, future, retired, revoked, superseded, missing, and terminal misuse fail exactly.
Supplied explicit time covers before, exact, after, expiry, freshness, compromise, and cross-phase boundaries without ambient clock use.
Historical, current, and acceptance inputs and verdicts remain exact and non-substitutable.
Zero, one, N, and N+1 candidate, byte, depth, member, row, finding, and aggregate limits run before parse, hash, crypto, or graph work.
Duplicate members, noncanonical data, unknown fields, wrong types, excessive depth, traversal, symlinks, binaries, and malformed encodings fail exactly.
Missing, extra, truncated, bit-flipped, hash-mismatched, and orphaned material cannot retain identity or eligibility.
Input permutations are deterministic while duplicate candidate, finding, graph, blob, and replay identities fail exactly.
Candidate, identity, signature, phase, scope, trust, authority, graph member, blob, and source substitutions fail at the earliest applicable stage.
Only an independently supplied key may verify a bound candidate; the exact candidate, signature, order, count, phase, and result are recorded.
Only an independently trusted candidate whose canonical identity appears in the external authorization set may reach graph/conflict processing.

Only trusted and authorized eligible candidates enter graph work; forks, precedence, and conflicts are permutation invariant. A cyclic predecessor attempt cannot satisfy predecessor-bound content identity and fails at canonical identity before graph work.
Missing, extra, corrupt, duplicate, reordered, substituted, cross-phase, and self-trust replay inputs reproduce exact identity, findings, and verdicts or fail exactly.
